I reviewed all four lemmas in the file (lines 1–85): `specIdeal_injective`, `comap_fromSpec`, `ambientHyperplane_comap_equation` and `section_hyperplane_equation`. I also used Grep to see where `specIdeal_injective` and `comap_fromSpec` are used elsewhere in the OAI tree.

The only overlap between proofs is the cancellation of `Scheme.ΓSpecIso` inv/hom. In `specIdeal_injective` it is the `he` step, `congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Iso.inv_hom_id ...)`. In `comap_fromSpec` it is `simp only [← CommRingCat.hom_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]`. Each is a single-line routine iso cancellation, and the two are set up differently (one with an explicit RingHom composition, one as an ideal map under `congr 1`). A shared lemma would only wrap existing API, which the rubric excludes.

`ambientHyperplane_comap_equation` already holds the shared reasoning: it is the chain from injectivity to the `comap_fromSpec` rewrite. `section_hyperplane_equation` reuses it instead of repeating it. In PointIdealMembership.lean, two other proofs follow the same `apply specIdeal_injective; rw [← comap_fromSpec, ...]` pattern. That pattern is a short preamble that depends on the target lemmas, and those proofs are in another file.

I found no nontrivial reasoning repeated within this file that would justify factoring out a new lemma.
